transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-12
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Anika Rao (Redwood SE), Martin Dupont (Aurelia - Head of Cloud Architecture), Sofia Romero (Aurelia - CISO), Tom Walker (Aurelia - DevOps), Elena Petrescu (Aurelia - Legal)
Recorded by: Fireflies

Summary (auto):
Quick security and compliance review focused on data residency / region pinning options for EU-only workloads. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private options, cross-border processing risk, sub-processor list, KMS/encryption, audit logs and RBAC/SSO. Agreed next steps to share SOC2 artifacts and an EU deployment diagram; follow-up demo of Private/VPC in EU region.

00:00:00 - Liam (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick intro then jump into the residency questions. Anika from our SE team will cover the technical flow.
00:00:20 - Martin (Aurelia): Hi, thanks. We're mainly here because our legal and security teams are pushing for EU-only processing for PII, and we want to understand how Redwood guarantees region pinning and what sub-processors might cause cross-border movement.
00:00:35 - Sofia (Aurelia): Also want to confirm encryption at rest with our KMS and whether Redwood ever holds keys.
00:00:45 - Liam (Redwood): Totally. Quick agenda: region pinning options, hosted vs dedicated vs private, KMS/keys, audit logs and SSO/RBAC. Then Q&A and next steps.
00:01:10 - Anika (Redwood): Great, I'll start with the high-level. So Redwood offers three main deployment modes: hosted (multi-tenant), dedicated/reserved, and private (VPC or on-prem). For EU-only residency the most common approach is either dedicated capacity in an EU region with region pinning, or Private in your VPC so data never leaves your network.
00:01:45 - Tom (Aurelia): When you say "region pinning" is that a hard guarantee? Like requests from EU go to EU compute and storage only?
00:02:05 - Anika (Redwood): Short answer: yes if configured. We have routing policies that pin requests to EU-backed clusters. In hosted mode we can pin to EU region clusters and avoid cross-region fallback. That said, there are caveats: for some managed services (analytics, logging retention) we provide configurable storage region settings but customers should validate any integrations that would export telemetry outside EU.
00:02:35 - Martin (Aurelia): What about metadata, logs, and metrics? Our DPO is worried about metadata being stored in US.
00:02:50 - Anika (Redwood): Good question. We separate control plane and data plane. For hosted customers some non-sensitive control-plane metadata (billing counters, aggregated telemetry) may be stored in central datastores; however for EU-residency accounts we provide options: either replicate control plane artifacts to EU-only datastores or enable privacy mode where we minimize control plane retention and send only aggregated metrics. For audit-grade needs, we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can host both control plane proxies and data plane inside your VPC/region.
00:03:25 - Sofia (Aurelia): If we pick hosted EU pinning, are there any sub-processors that could trigger data transfer? Do you have a list?
00:03:40 - Liam (Redwood): Yes we maintain a sub-processor list. We'll share the latest PDF and the SOC2 Type II report. Typical sub-processors include cloud providers (GCP, Azure in EU regions), analytics providers, and a few CDNs. We also have partners for telemetry; for EU contracts we can restrict to EU-only sub-processors or include standard SCCs.
00:04:05 - Elena (Aurelia): Are you willing to sign data processing addendum (DPA) with EU-only subprocessing commitments?
00:04:20 - Liam (Redwood): Yes, we have a DPA template and can include region pinning clauses and sub-processor controls.
00:04:30 - 00:04:45 - Speaker change / small crosstalk
00:04:45 - Anika (Redwood): I'll show an architecture sketch \u000B (there is a link in chat) \u000B For EU pinning in hosted: requests route to EU load balancer -> EU inference pool -> KV cache and object store in EU. For secrets, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in your KMS \u000B Redwood can support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) via KMS integrations so we never hold plaintext keys.
00:05:25 - Tom (Aurelia): Can we use our own KMS (Azure Key Vault / AWS KMS) so Redwood never has decrypt rights?
00:05:40 - Anika (Redwood): Yes, we support KMS integrations. Two common patterns: envelope encryption where Redwood stores encrypted model artifacts/objects but decryption requires a key retrieval step from your KMS; or full in-VPC private deployment where keys never leave your environment. There may be some tradeoffs on startup latency for models if the key unwrap happens frequently, but we have caching patterns for unwrap tokens.
00:06:15 - Martin (Aurelia): How about audit logs? We need immutable logs for requests, response hashes, who accessed what and when. Retention 7 years for some data.
00:06:35 - Anika (Redwood): We provide request/response-level audit logs for Private deployments and for Dedicated we can enable detailed logging with S3-compatible object retention in your EU bucket. For hosted customers we can stream audit logs to customer-owned endpoints (SQS/Kafka/S3) in EU. Retention policies are configurable. For immutability we recommend storing logs in append-only object store with Object Lock (GCP/Azure/AWS) under customer account.
00:07:10 - Sofia (Aurelia): Any chance model outputs (generated text) might be used for model-retraining or telemetry that leaves the EU?
00:07:25 - Anika (Redwood): By default hosted telemetry may be used for platform improvements in anonymized ways; however for customers with strict residency we have an opt-out and data-use restrict mode which prevents outputs and prompt content from being used for any model training or external analytics. In Dedicated/Private modes there is no sharing unless you opt in.
00:07:55 - Martin (Aurelia): We need proof \u000B examples in SLAs or contracts.
00:08:10 - Liam (Redwood): We'll include specific contract language in the DPA and can add SLA runbooks for fallback behavior. We'll circulate the SOC 2 artifacts and the DPA redline.
00:08:25 - 00:08:40 - (background noise; brief pause)
00:08:40 - Tom (Aurelia): Regarding SSO and RBAC, we require SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning, plus fine-grained roles for who can call inference endpoints and who can view audit logs.
00:08:55 - Anika (Redwood): Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. For RBAC we have role templates and custom roles \u000B Admin, Developer, Auditor, ReadOnly, etc. You can map groups via SAML assertions. For API-level controls we support per-route API keys and token scoping.
00:09:25 - Sofia (Aurelia): Is there separation between billing and data access? We don't want billing-only teams to be able to see raw prompts/outputs.
00:09:40 - Anika (Redwood): Yes, we can separate billing metadata from content. Billing owners only see usage aggregates. Access to raw transcripts/requests is gated by RBAC/Audit role.
00:09:55 - Martin (Aurelia): If we choose Dedicated capacity in EU, what's the path and timeline?
00:10:10 - Liam (Redwood): Typical flow: contract + DPA signed, provisioning dedicated GPU pool in EU region (2-4 weeks depending on capacity), network peering/VPC setup (1-2 weeks), security review + Staging PoC (2-4 weeks). For acceleration we can offer an express onboarding option but it requires a larger commit.
00:10:40 - Martin (Aurelia): Can we do an initial hosted EU pinned PoC to validate latency before committing to Dedicated?
00:10:55 - Anika (Redwood): Absolutely. Hosted EU pinning is how many customers prototype. We'll lock routing to EU region and provide a test dataset. Note: we will disable cross-region fallback for that PoC.
00:11:15 - Elena (Aurelia): About sub-processors again: do you have any US-based subsidiaries that might access data?
00:11:30 - Liam (Redwood): We do have engineering teams in US, but with EU-residency we can restrict operational access and provide just-in-time access controls with HIPAA/ISO/SOC-approved processes. For highly restricted accounts we can enable private deployment so engineering does not access raw data.
00:11:55 - 00:12:10 - (brief mic drop / laugh)
00:12:10 - Sofia (Aurelia): Encryption in transit \u000B TLS only? Perfect forward secrecy?
00:12:25 - Anika (Redwood): All ingress/egress is TLS1.2+ with modern ciphers and PFS. Internally we also encrypt data in transit between services.
00:12:40 - Martin (Aurelia): For on-prem option, is the control plane still Redwood-managed?
00:12:55 - Anika (Redwood): We offer a private control plane option where the control plane is customer-managed in their VPC; Redwood provides images and automation to run the control plane. For air-gapped/on-prem we have a separate engagement and it's typically a longer project with an enterprise license.
00:13:20 - Tom (Aurelia): How do you handle KV cache and models \u000B are model shards or cache persisted to object store in EU only?
00:13:35 - Anika (Redwood): Yes in EU pinning we persist KV cache and model artifacts to EU object stores. For ephemeral caches we use in-region memory/GPU. If using Dedicated/Private we can configure retention and TTLs in your EU buckets.
00:13:55 - Martin (Aurelia): Any third-party monitoring agents that phone home?
00:14:10 - Anika (Redwood): We avoid any default "phone home" agents. Monitoring is via metrics endpoints and logs. For hosted customers we offer metric collection; for EU-restricted customers we can route monitoring to customer-owned endpoints only.
00:14:30 - Liam (Redwood): Quick note \u000B we've seen customers ask for contractual guarantees around no cross-border transfers except for explicit exceptions. We can include that language and standard SCCs in the DPA.
00:14:45 - Sofia (Aurelia): What about law enforcement or government requests? Where would those be processed?
00:15:00 - Liam (Redwood): We comply with lawful requests per our legal process; for EU-hosted data we would route legal process through our EU office where possible and notify customers unless prohibited. We can include transparency in the DPA. For the strictest cases, Private on-prem keeps data under customer control.
00:15:25 - 00:15:40 - (typing sounds)
00:15:40 - Martin (Aurelia): Do you provide TLS certs management or do we bring our own certs?
00:15:55 - Anika (Redwood): Both. We can manage certs and use Let's Encrypt or CA, or you can bring your own certificates via ACM/Key Vault and we will use them on the load balancer.
00:16:15 - Tom (Aurelia): On the topic of observability, can audit logs be exported to our SIEM which is in EU?
00:16:30 - Anika (Redwood): Yes \u000B we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure connectors, or you can pull logs from EU S3 buckets.
00:16:45 - Martin (Aurelia): Is there any scenario where fallback would route to a non-EU region automatically? E.g., under load or failover?
00:17:00 - Anika (Redwood): By default we have regional fallback for availability; however for pinned accounts we can disable cross-region fallback and instead fail closed or use local degraded capacity. This is a policy you set per environment. We'll show the configuration options in the runbook.
00:17:25 - Sofia (Aurelia): Would disabling cross-region fallback increase risk of downtime?
00:17:40 - Anika (Redwood): Yes there's a tradeoff. If you disable fallback you accept potential availability impact during region outages. Many customers choose a hybrid: keep EU-only for production, but have a DR plan with contractual constraints or an explicit emergency process.
00:17:58 - 00:18:10 - (short pause)
00:18:10 - Liam (Redwood): Can I ask about compliance frameworks you care about? We support SOC2, ISO27001, and we have documentation for PCI/PD/financial compliance patterns.
00:18:25 - Elena (Aurelia): We require SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 evidence and prefer vendors with strong artifact retention. Also we need contractual PCI scope reduction guidance.
00:18:40 - Liam (Redwood): We'll send SOC2 Type II and ISO summary. For PCI we have guidelines for tokenization and scope reduction.
00:18:55 - Martin (Aurelia): On data deletion \u000B if we ask to delete EU customer data, how is that processed and proven?
00:19:10 - Anika (Redwood): Deletion is handled via delete APIs and background jobs; for EU buckets we can perform object lifecycle deletes and return an attestable deletion report. For backups we can provide a deletion schedule and attestations.
00:19:30 - Tom (Aurelia): What about backups that might be stored in other regions by default?
00:19:45 - Anika (Redwood): For EU-resident accounts we can configure backup targets to be EU-only and disable cross-region replication.
00:20:00 - 00:20:15 - (minor overlap from another participant)
00:20:15 - Martin (Aurelia): Are there any performance impacts with EU-only KMS calls or CMK unwraps?
00:20:30 - Anika (Redwood): There can be slight latency at cold start during key unwraps; we mitigate with short-lived unwrap tokens and local cache. For high-throughput workloads we recommend Dedicated with local key caching or Private in-VPC key management.
00:20:50 - Sofia (Aurelia): For legal/regulatory proof, do you provide an architecture attestation or a questionnaire response?
00:21:05 - Liam (Redwood): We usually provide an architecture diagram, SOC2 report, ISO docs, and a vendor security questionnaire (e.g., SIG) responses. We'll pre-fill parts of the questionnaire for speed.
00:21:25 - Anika (Redwood): I'm going to call out a couple of gotchas: analytics/monitoring vendors and CI/CD integrations often cause accidental egress. When you sign the DPA we can list forbidden integrations and secure channels.
00:21:50 - Martin (Aurelia): Good to know. We saw one vendor leak metadata via their error reporting tool.
00:22:05 - Liam (Redwood): We'll also add a recommended network policy sample for egress controls.
00:22:15 - 00:22:30 - (pause, someone joins late)
00:22:30 - New Speaker: Hi apologies I'm late \u000B quick Q: are you supporting EU data residency in both GCP and Azure?
00:22:45 - Anika (Redwood): Yes, we run in multiple clouds. EU residency can be satisfied in GCP-eu, AWS-eu or Azure EU regions. We'll include region mapping doc.
00:22:58 - Martin (Aurelia): For logging, can we require logs be stored in our customer-owned bucket rather than Redwood-managed?
00:23:15 - Anika (Redwood): Yes, streaming to customer-owned buckets is standard for compliance customers.
00:23:30 - Sofia (Aurelia): About encryption keys again \u000B if Redwood manages the key, is there separation of duties so devops can't decrypt production PII?
00:23:45 - Anika (Redwood): We implement key access policies and just-in-time access; if you want strict separation we recommend customer-managed keys or Private deployment.
00:24:00 - Liam (Redwood): Quick note on pricing: Dedicated and Private have different pricing/commits; security-heavy accounts often go Dedicated or Private. We'll put estimates in the follow-up.
00:24:15 - 00:24:30 - (laugh)
00:24:30 - Tom (Aurelia): One more \u000B do you have an EU-based DPO contact for legal inquiries?
00:24:45 - Liam (Redwood): Yes, we'll connect you with our EU DPO.
00:24:55 - Anika (Redwood): I'm going to call out some concrete config knobs: route_policy=eu_only; control_plane_mode=localized; log_sink=customer_s3_eu; kms_mode=customer_managed. We'll share the runbook with sample commands.
00:25:20 - Martin (Aurelia): For the PoC, what is the simplest config to prove no cross-border egress?
00:25:35 - Anika (Redwood): Spin up a hosted EU-pinned instance with route_policy=eu_only, disable telemetry export, set log_sink to your EU bucket, and use a CMK. We'll run test vectors and you can validate egress via packet captures or logs.
00:25:55 - Sofia (Aurelia): Can you provide a test harness or script to validate egress?
00:26:10 - Anika (Redwood): Yes \u000B we have a small egress test toolkit that pings endpoints and checks headers and S3 writes; we'll share it.
00:26:25 - Liam (Redwood): I'll note that the legal team often asks for a clause about sub-processors being approved in advance; we can include a 30-day notification for new sub-processors.
00:26:40 - Elena (Aurelia): That would be helpful.
00:26:50 - 00:27:05 - (keyboard clacking)
00:27:05 - Martin (Aurelia): Regarding backups and DR, is cross-region replication disabled by default for EU accounts?
00:27:20 - Anika (Redwood): Not disabled by default, but we set it per account. For EU-only accounts we disable replication unless the customer requests DR replication to a designated EU region.
00:27:40 - Tom (Aurelia): How do you show proof of encryption at rest per object?
00:27:55 - Anika (Redwood): We publish encryption metadata per object and can provide attestations showing CMK IDs and envelope encryption details.
00:28:10 - Sofia (Aurelia): Is there a sandbox we can use that mirrors EU policy?
00:28:25 - Liam (Redwood): Yes, we can provision a sandbox with identical policy; we'll do that for the PoC.
00:28:35 - Anika (Redwood): Also note: function/tool-calling and streaming are supported in EU region; there are no feature differences except where third-party integrations exist.
00:28:55 - 00:29:10 - (small noise)
00:29:10 - Martin (Aurelia): If we want to redact PII before logs leave our systems, can we plug in a pre-processing filter?
00:29:25 - Anika (Redwood): Yes \u000B Redwood supports pre-processing hooks where you can run a redaction function (lambda-like) before persistence. This can run in your VPC for full control.
00:29:45 - Sofia (Aurelia): Do you support SIEM connectors like Splunk or Elastic in EU?
00:29:58 - Anika (Redwood): Yes, Splunk/Elastic connectors supported and can be configured to point only to EU endpoints.
00:30:15 - Liam (Redwood): We're nearing the end of time, quick recap?
00:30:25 - Martin (Aurelia): We want a PoC with EU pinning, SOC2 artifacts, sub-processor list, and DPA. We'll provide data classification and timeline.
00:30:40 - Liam (Redwood): Action items: we'll share SOC2/ISO docs and sub-processor list (Liam), Anika will prepare EU architecture diagram and runbook and the egress test toolkit, Martin will confirm data classes.
00:30:58 - 00:31:10 - (agreement)
00:31:10 - Elena (Aurelia): One legal question \u000B are you open to adding a clause for no non-EU sub-processors without written consent?
00:31:25 - Liam (Redwood): Yes we can discuss that in the DPA but would need to surface any operational exceptions; we'll provide redlines.
00:31:40 - Sofia (Aurelia): Great. Also please include a sample incident response playbook for region failover.
00:31:55 - Anika (Redwood): We'll attach an incident playbook sample.
00:32:05 - Tom (Aurelia): For the PoC we'll need credentials and a short onboarding doc.
00:32:20 - Liam (Redwood): We'll send a quickstart and test credentials scoped to the sandbox.
00:32:35 - 00:32:50 - (typing)
00:32:50 - Martin (Aurelia): Anything else on encryption or keys we should worry about?
00:33:05 - Anika (Redwood): Just to reiterate: prefer CMK + short-lived tokens + local unwrap caching for performance and security. We'll include perf numbers in follow-up.
00:33:25 - Liam (Redwood): Okay, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone \u000B we'll follow up with artifacts tomorrow.
00:33:35 - Sofia (Aurelia): Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
00:33:40 - Elena (Aurelia): Thanks all.
00:33:45 - Tom (Aurelia): Thanks.
00:33:50 - 00:34:05 - (call ends)
